problem.statement: WPF TextBlocks that bind a changing Text property to a StaticResource FontFamily leak unmanaged UnmanagedMemoryStream font allocations on every text change, growing memory without bound in long-running apps.

persona.primary: WPF/.NET developer maintaining a long-running desktop application

context.situation: A .NET 7 WPF developer instrumented their app, found font-backed UnmanagedMemoryStream objects were never disposed on repeated Text updates, and filed a public bug report with a repro but no known fix.

possible_wedges.offer: Static analyzer that scans WPF XAML/codebehind for FontFamily+bound-Text patterns known to leak unmanaged font memory, as part of a legacy-app audit report.
Runtime memory diagnostic that attaches to a running WPF app and flags undisposed UnmanagedMemoryStream/font allocations growing over time.
Manual legacy WPF codebase audit that checks for this and similar unmanaged-resource leak patterns as a paid one-off engagement.

risks: Single evidence source: one GitHub issue, no corroborating reports
No workarounds or commercial-intent signals present (commercial_intent scored only 0.1)
Unclear how widespread the pattern (StaticResource FontFamily + bound Text) is in real production apps vs. this one repro
Microsoft could patch this in a future .NET/WPF runtime release, making third-party detection tooling short-lived
No indication anyone would pay for detection vs. just reporting/upvoting the bug

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers maintaining long-running desktop apps will engage with a free diagnostic checklist/script for this leak pattern, signaling latent demand for audit tooling.
cheapest_experiment.input: A short writeup with the repro pattern and a free memory-leak detection script, posted to WPF/.NET developer communities (e.g. r/dotnet, WPF Discord, relevant GitHub issue threads).
cheapest_experiment.output: Downloads/comments on the script plus replies confirming they hit this issue in their own app.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: A developer asks to be notified when a full audit tool is available or requests a paid codebase scan.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: 10+ meaningful replies or script downloads with at least 2 requests for a paid/early-access audit within 2 weeks
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: Fewer than 3 replies or no requests for further tooling after 2 weeks
